evidence:
Most of the 54 criteria are sound for this row: outcomes are read from the rendered editor, console, preview, library and history; negatives carry a working control (format error, isolation, dynamic code, stop, supersede, newer-revision baseline); probes are distinctive (computed sums, markers joined from two halves, dot/bracket and case decoys, '>' inside an attribute value); durable state is re-read in a third page and after restart_app. No criterion asks for a source read; the constraints gate reads live DOM only. The visual likert rows are subjective by template design. Instances that do not meet the row, all in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml unless stated:

(1) cw_history_restore_retry, line 371 - the idempotency probe is not distinctive. 'Then send that same already completed restore request a second time. If the app offers a control for retrying it, use it and confirm in the network activity that a second restore request was actually sent ... After the second request no fifth revision may exist.' The ordinary Restore control satisfies the stated test for a retry control (it visibly re-sends a restore request for revision one), but a second user Restore is a new operation that the public contract REQUIRES to add a revision (behaviour.md: 'Restoring an older snapshot creates a new current revision of the same record'). The judge in the hosted run on the earlier candidate did exactly this: 'A second full UI restore of revision 1 - a distinct legit action I performed - created revision 5; the retry mechanism itself added none.' It only reached the right verdict because the golden happens to ship a separate 'Retry same restore' button (solution/app/src/app.tsx:163); the public notes do not require such a control. The same sentence also later assumes exactly four revisions ('save a fifth revision from the first tab'), which the extra legit restore breaks (that run ended at revisions 6 and 7). In addition, the escape clause 'say so and leave this one step out without failing the criterion for it' makes the idempotency outcome ungraded for any app whose restore is not a replayable HTTP request.

(2) cw_find_forward_backward_wrap, line 137 - 'Fails ... if matches are only decorated and never become the current selection' has no probe that can tell the two apart. In an own-drawn editor a selection is itself a decoration; keyboard focus stays in the Find field during Next/Previous, so the 'copied' alternative copies from the Find field, and the criterion accepts 'the line readout and the copied or highlighted text'. The earlier hosted judge passed on 'Each current match was the active hit with exact text ... and matching Ln/Col readout', i.e. on the highlight class and readout only. No other criterion proves the public rule 'The current match is selected in the editor' (cw_replace_current can work from a match index).

(3) cw_mouse_selection, line 56 - 'a drag from the middle of one line to the middle of the next must select exactly the text between those two points' gives the judge no way to fix the two points to character boundaries, so 'exactly' is not decidable. The earlier hosted judge passed with 'a contiguous range between the two clicked points (within +-1 char of my pixel-coordinate precision)'. The double-click and triple-click legs are decidable.

(4) cw_undo_restores_caret, line 128 - 'immediately type one character: it must be inserted ... at the exact place where the first marker had begun, and the line and column readout must show that position'. After the character is typed a correct readout shows that column plus one (earlier hosted run: 'Ln 2, Col 8' before, 'Ln 2, Col 9' after). The sentence does not say which moment is meant.

(5) cw_block_indent_undo, line 74 - 'ends at column zero of the following third line' while the public readout is one-based ('the start of the document reads line 1, column 1', ui.md). Wording only; low impact.

(6) cw_stop_cancels_pending_work line 308 and cw_newer_run_supersedes line 317 - the outcome depends on judge latency inside a 4 s window, and two void attempts fail the app ('fail this criterion and say that Stop could not be pressed in time'). The earlier hosted judge managed 146 ms and 286 ms by batching the actions, so this is a risk and not a demonstrated defect; it is unmeasured on these bytes. cw_output_before_failure_kept line 254 has the same Stop-before-4-s leg with no void rule: a late Stop silently turns that leg into a normal completed run.

(7) tests/scored/polish/judge.toml cw_controls_feedback_and_labels, line 32 - 'the main controls have understandable visible names' is a judgement with no listed set of controls or probe; the three feedback legs are decidable.

Evidence limits: no configured judge run exists for these bytes; the scripted golden results say nothing about how an LLM judge reads these sentences. The quoted judge observations come from the earlier candidate (ZIP eda58464) whose criteria were reworded afterwards.
counterexample: Conforming app that could fail (instance 1): an app that implements restore idempotency with a client operation id and has only a Restore button, no separate retry button. The judge, told to use 'a control for retrying it' and to 'confirm in the network activity that a second restore request was actually sent', presses Restore on revision one again, sees a second restore request and a legitimate fifth revision, and applies 'Fails ... if the repeated request adds a revision'. The earlier hosted judge performed this very action and got a fifth revision from the golden. Broken app that could pass (instance 2): an app that paints the current find hit with a highlight span and updates the line/column readout but never changes the editor selection (typing after returning to the editor inserts at the old caret instead of replacing the match) passes cw_find_forward_backward_wrap on 'highlighted text' plus readout. Broken app that could pass (instance 3): a drag selection that is one character short or long at either end passes under the +-1 character tolerance the judge had to allow itself.
suggested_fix: (1) State that pressing the ordinary Restore control again is a new restore and is not the retry; define the retry as either a control the app itself labels as a retry of the same attempt or the replay of the recorded request, and say that revision counts in the later steps are relative to the revisions that then exist. Decide whether the idempotency step may really be skipped; if it may, say that the criterion then grades only the remaining steps. (2) Add a probe for the selection: after a match is current, return to the editor with the keyboard as the app shows on screen (or copy with the editor focused) and confirm the copied text equals the literal, or type one character and confirm it replaces exactly that match, then Undo; otherwise drop the 'only decorated' fail condition. (3) Tell the judge to aim the drag at character boundaries it has read from the rendered text positions and to state the expected text from them, or to confirm the drag start and end with the line/column readout. (4) Say the readout shows the marker's start position before the character is typed and one column further after it. (5) Write 'the start of the following third line'. (6) and (7) Record as risks; name the controls meant by 'main controls'.
